role: Senior positions in economic development and reform, project finance, private-sector development, telecommunications privatisation and infrastructure
description: About fifteen years at the World Bank Group, according to Wikipedia; the dates here follow WAFA's profile, which gives 1991–2005 for his work abroad before he joined the Palestine Investment Fund. During a sabbatical from the Bank he was the founding chief executive of the Palestine Telecommunications Company (Paltel), according to Wikipedia citing Bloomberg; WAFA describes him as a driving force behind Paltel's establishment. He also advised the Government of Kuwait on economic reform and Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (two years each, per Wikipedia), held private-sector positions in Kuwait, the US and Palestine, and was a visiting professor at George Washington University.

role: Senior economic adviser to the President
organization: Office of the President of the Palestinian National Authority (President Mahmoud Abbas)
description: Abbas's senior economic adviser from 2005, according to Al-Monitor, until his appointment as Prime Minister; The Times of Israel described him in 2022 as Abbas's 'longtime chief economic adviser'.

Chief executive of the PIF, the PA's sovereign investment fund, from 2006 to 2013 according to WAFA (the ICIJ dates his appointment to 2005). WAFA credits him with launching companies and funds including the Palestinian National Mobile Company (Wataniya, 2008), the Amaar real estate company (2009), the Rasmala Palestinian Equity Fund (2011) and Palestine Power Generation. From March 2006 he also sat, representing the PIF's shares, on the board of the Arab Palestinian Investment (Holding) Company, registered in the British Virgin Islands (see polemics).

role: Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs
organization: 15th and 16th Palestinian governments (Prime Minister Rami Hamdallah)
description: Joined the government in 2013 as Deputy Prime Minister for economic affairs (ICIJ; WAFA). Dates from Wikipedia.

role: Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy
organization: 17th Palestinian government (national consensus government of Prime Minister Rami Hamdallah)
description: Held both posts in the consensus government formed in June 2014 and was put in charge of Gaza's reconstruction after the 2014 war, leading the ministerial committee at the 2014 Cairo donors' conference. He submitted his resignation on 31 March 2015, officially for personal reasons (see polemics). WAFA lists him as Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy in the 16th and 17th governments (2014–2015); the dates here follow Wikipedia.

role: Chairman of the board of directors
description: Chairman of the PIF from 2015 until he became Prime Minister, according to WAFA; under him the fund became a full member of the International Forum of Sovereign Wealth Funds. WAFA also lists him as Palestine's governor at the Arab Fund for Economic and Social Development and as a trustee of the Institute for Palestine Studies and the Yasser Arafat Foundation.

role: Member of the Executive Committee, head of its Economic Department
description: Elected by the PLO Central Council in February 2022 to the seat left by Hanan Ashrawi; WAFA describes him as an independent member heading the Executive Committee's Economic Department.

organization: State of Palestine / Palestinian National Authority
description: Designated by President Abbas on 14 March 2024 after the resignation of Mohammad Shtayyeh's government, he presented his cabinet and programme on 28 March, when Abbas granted confidence by decree, and was sworn in with 23 ministers on 31 March 2024. Reshuffles: the foreign ministry passed to Varsen Aghabekian on 23 June 2025 and the finance ministry from Omar al-Bitar to Estephan Salameh (also in charge of planning) in November 2025. As of 22 October 2026 he remains in office.

role: Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates
description: Kept the foreign ministry for himself when forming his government, with Varsen Aghabekian as Minister of State for Foreign Affairs; on 23 June 2025 Abbas approved a reshuffle in which she became foreign minister.

role: Head of the Palestinian Authority's Liaison Office with the Office of the High Representative for Gaza
description: Vice-President Hussein al-Sheikh informed the Board of Peace's High Representative for Gaza, Nickolay Mladenov, on 21 February 2026 that the PA had set up a liaison office under Mustafa's leadership to coordinate on the US 20-point plan and UN Security Council Resolution 2803.
